findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap() on fallible file I/O with no error handling
findings.failure_mode: Corrupted, missing, or unreadable file path causes an unconditional thread panic, crashing the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error the caller can handle
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> (or a domain-typed error enum) and propagate with ? or map_err

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) inside a .map() closure — hidden I/O side effect inside a data-transform pipeline
findings.failure_mode: Violates functional-core separation; the function has observable side effects that make it non-deterministic from the caller's perspective, breaks pure-core assumption, and produces console output on every invocation (including in tests and benchmarks) which cannot be suppressed or audited
findings.fix: Remove the println entirely, or extract I/O into a separate shell/action layer that receives pure records and handles logging there

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 — unwrap() on parse + lossy as cast from u32 to u16
findings.failure_mode: Two failure modes: (1) non-numeric field value panics instead of returning a typed parse error, (2) values in u32 range [65536..=4294967295] silently truncate on the as cast to u16, producing incorrect data without any signal that data loss occurred
findings.fix: Parse into u16 directly with .parse::<u16>()?, or parse to u32 then convert with u16::try_from(parsed)? and return a typed Overflow error on failure

findings.problem: parts[0] — direct indexing on a Vec with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: If a line is empty or contains no comma, parts has fewer than 2 elements and this indexing panics at runtime instead of returning a typed MalformedLine error
findings.fix: Use parts.first() and parts.get(1) with ? or map_err to convert None into a typed ParseError for the line

findings.problem: parts[1] — direct indexing on a Vec with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: Same as line 16 — a line with zero or one comma produces a Vec with length 1, and indexing parts[1] panics
findings.fix: Use parts.get(1) with ? or map_err into a typed error

findings.problem: Unbounded collect into Vec<String> from splitting every line — no domain cap on session count, no try_reserve, no streaming
findings.failure_mode: A malicious or extremely large file causes unbounded heap allocation proportional to file size with no upper limit. An attacker can supply a gigabyte file and trigger OOM before any record is validated or processed
findings.fix: Validate a MAX_SESSIONS constant before parsing, use try_reserve against that cap, or stream line-by-line and yield Results with an iterator that caps total records

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 with pub fields — no newtypes, no invariants, no type-level constraints on name or value
findings.failure_mode: Any code can construct Record { name: String::new(), value: 0 } or any invalid combination. The name has no non-empty or length invariant, value has no domain range check, and pub fields allow unsanitized mutation from any module
findings.fix: Introduce newtypes like SessionName(String) with a smart constructor that validates, make fields private with a constructor returning Result, or use a non-empty-string newtype and add a value-range invariant

findings.problem: use std::fs at module level — the function fuses I/O and parsing in a single public API with no separation of concerns
findings.failure_mode: The shell (file reading) and core (parsing/transforming) are inseparable. The function cannot be unit-tested without real filesystem access, cannot be composed with other data sources (API, env, network), and couples the parser to a specific I/O modality
findings.fix: Split into parse_sessions(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> (pure core) and load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> (shell that reads and delegates to core)

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions allocation or throughput
no profiler evidence for hot-path analysis of the parsing pipeline
no allocation budget analysis for the unbounded Vec collect
no command evidence (cargo fmt/check/clippy/test) was run
no MAX_SESSIONS or domain cap constant defined anywhere in the crate
residual_risk: Static review only — no commands run. The crate contains 5 BLOCKER violations (unwrap on I/O and parse, lossy cast, unchecked indexing, unbounded allocation) and 2 WARNING violations (raw domain types, fused shell/core). All unwrap calls on hostile input and the lossy cast must be fixed before the function can be considered safe for any external use.
